thread:
maria: Heads-up — ACME (tenant acme-corp) says their monthly credits "refreshed" at 00:03 instead of 00:00 local time. They reported app chime and UI showing 0 -> full at 00:03 PST. Can we triage?

ashwin: Do we have logs / exact timestamps? Is this a display-only issue or did credits actually get applied late? :thinking_face:

maria: I grabbed the billing-worker logs from that window. Snippet:```
2026-03-17T07:00:00.001Z billing-worker INFO start reset tenant=acme-corp tz=America/Los_Angeles
2026-03-17T07:00:00.450Z billing-worker INFO compute_next_window tenant=acme-corp window=2026-03-17T07:00:00Z
2026-03-17T07:00:03.120Z billing-worker INFO write_credits tenant=acme-corp credits=5000 tx=0xabc123
2026-03-17T07:00:03.125Z notify-service INFO emit tenant=acme-corp event=credits_refreshed
```
Looks like billing write did happen at 07:00:03Z which is 00:00:03 PST, but the customer sees 00:03 local — customer says they heard the chime at 00:03, UI shows the same. Might be a downstream retry/fanout delay?

lucas: Two quick asks: 1) Is the billing-worker single-shard job or fanout per-project? 2) What triggers the UI chime? Is it websocket event or a separate poll?

maria: 1) Single-shard per-tenant, but it enqueues per-project updates after the tenant write. 2) UI chime is driven by notification-service which subscribes to expired-cache events and webhooks + websocket fanout.

sarah: Could be the notification-service backpressure. We've seen a backlog spike when many tenants reset simultaneously (end-of-month). Check notification queue depth around that time.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: Noted — notification-service had a 30s GC pause on 2026-03-17T07:00:01Z in eu-west-1 (GC pause 28s) during a config roll.

ashwin: That GC pause aligns with the 3s write and the chime at 00:03 local — but 3s vs 3 minutes mismatch. Customer claims 3 minutes not 3 seconds. Any other retries or exponential backoff?

maria: Good catch. I checked the notification consumer metrics: we saw initial emit at 07:00:03Z but the socket push to that customer's long-lived websocket failed (connection reset) and retried with increasing backoff: first retry at 07:01:00Z, second at 07:02:15Z, third at 07:03:01Z — the client received the push at 07:03:01Z -> 00:03:01 PST. So the observable chime was when the push succeeded, not the credit write.

lucas: So root cause: credit write is fine, but websocket push retries + client reconnect made the UX look like a late reset. Is that consistent across other tenants?

maria: We checked 20 tenants in the same shard — 18 had same pattern (write at 07:00:0xZ, client reception up to ~07:03Z for clients with flaky ws). A few clients on mobile (sleeping sockets) got it much later.

sarah: Actionable mitigation: 1) Make UI derive balance from the credits API on page load (poll once) instead of relying solely on push chime. 2) Ensure notification-service emits an eventual 'credits_refreshed' event that persists for N minutes so clients can request the canonical state.

ashwin: Short-term support playbook: tell customer credits were applied at 00:00:03 and provide logs. Recommend refreshing the page or calling GET /v1/tenants/{id}/credits to see authoritative state. Long-term: change notify flow.

maria: Drafted customer reply: "Thanks — we confirm credits were written at 00:00:03 PST. The chime you heard at 00:03 was a delayed websocket retry. We're rolling out a fix to surface authoritative balances via the API and to make notification delivery more resilient. Apologies for the confusion." Thoughts?

lucas: LGTM. Also add a monitoring alert for websocket retry spikes at month boundaries.

support-bot: ticket #INC-2026-478 created and assigned to @ashwin. ETA for customer-facing fix: next week canary, full rollout in 2 sprints.

maria: I'll send the logs and repro steps to the ticket. Repro steps for SRE/dev:```
1) Set tenant tz: `PATCH /v1/tenants/acme-corp {"timezone":"America/Los_Angeles"}`
2) Advance billing-worker in staging: `./billing-sim --tenant acme-corp --advance-rollover 2026-03-17T07:00:00Z`
3) Kill websocket for a test client or simulate network flaps to reproduce retry behavior.
4) Observe notification-service consumer logs and websocket push timings.```

sarah: Will add a short runbook entry. :white_check_mark:

maria: Thanks all. I'll update the customer and close the loop once ashwin confirms the ticket and timeline. :pray:
